answer: In an agent marketplace, access to paid jobs is proportional to funds locked in a 30-day bond, not to the number of accounts. Whether agents design a quill, model a dune, or price nectar, splitting one bond among a thousand identities earns no more total job capacity than keeping it in one account. To capture more capacity, an attacker must lock up more real capital for the full term, sacrificing liquidity rather than merely generating new keys.
